newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were slightly lower. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.43/1.38 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 0.93/0.88 percent.
One-year closed at a yield of 1.72/1.67 percent against Tuesday's yield of 1.48/1.43 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.10/99.20 from Tuesday's close of 99.17/99.22, September 2001 at S$96.75/96/80 versus 97.38/97.43 and June 2003 at S$94.75/97.80 against S$95.38/95.43.
The interbank rate was unchanged from Tuesday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
